column3: “Caused to go up … from on to the wall” is rendered “had … come up on top of the wall.” “Two great thanksgiving choirs and processions” is rendered “two great choirs, the first proceeding”; the Hebrew is difficult. “The gate of the dung” is rendered “the Refuse Gate.”
“Brothers” is rendered “kinsmen,” and “the instruments of the song” as “the musical instruments.” NASB supplies “went.”
“Before themselves” is rendered “directly,” and “the ascent” as “the stairway.”
“To the front” is rendered “to the left”; the Hebrew word may mean “opposite,” and the meaning is uncertain. “The tower of the ovens” is rendered “the Tower of Furnaces.”
“The gate of the Jeshanah” is rendered “the Old Gate.”
“They caused to hear” is rendered “sang.” NASB spells “Jezrahiah,” and “the overseer” is rendered “their leader.”
“Made them rejoice a great joy” is rendered “had given them great joy.”
“The rooms for the stores” is rendered “the chambers for the stores”; NASB supplies “required.” “The joy of Judah was on” is rendered “Judah rejoiced over,” and “who were standing” as “who served.”
“Kept the service of their God” is rendered “performed the worship of their God”; NASB supplies “and of.”
“The matter of a day in its day” is rendered “as each day required”; NASB supplies “the consecrated portion.”
